cases.prompt: Photorealistic full-body photograph of the woman from <image1>, standing upright facing the camera with her arms relaxed and hanging at her sides with a small gap from her body, and her feet about shoulder width apart. Keep her face, hair, hair colour and skin tone exactly as in <image1>. She wears a plain light-grey t-shirt and dark trousers. cases.verdict: Pose from words only: correct stance (arms at sides, feet apart). Identity carried the reference's distinctive updo but the reference is a PROFILE view while the prompt asks for a frontal pose, so the head angle did not match the reference.

cases.prompt: Photorealistic full-body photograph of the woman from <image2>, standing in the exact pose shown in <image1> - the same stance, the same limb positions and the same body angles. cases.verdict: FAILED as a pose-transfer mechanism: the output is the PLATE's person reproduced wholesale (same man, same pose, same clothing) and the identity reference in <image2> had no effect. A photoreal full-body person in <image1> is treated as the base image to reproduce, not as a pose donor.

The figure adopts the skeleton's splayed arms and wide stance rather than reproducing a person. An OpenPose skeleton in a reference slot acts as POSE GUIDANCE.

Same seed and identical wording as the standing-skeleton case, and the prompt still says standing, yet the output follows the KNEELING skeleton: kneeling, both arms raised overhead, knees apart - exactly that skeleton's geometry. The pose comes from the skeleton image, overriding both the seed and the explicit word standing.

cases.verdict: Same three inputs in the LOCATION's own wide frame (1216x832): room, pose and identity all still land, so the earlier wide-frame identity loss is specific to the EDIT path with an angle-mismatched reference, not to generation-with-references. Known framing flaw: the wide stance pushes the left arm to the frame edge and crops the feet - the caller should pick a pose/framing combination that fits.

She wears a plain light-grey t-shirt and dark jeans. Keep her build and scale natural for the room. Sharp focus, natural skin texture, shot on 50mm.
cases.verdict: Slot-ORDER probe: the FACE as image_1, then pose, then location. Room, pose and identity all still landed, so in a 3-reference composition the order did NOT change the outcome. This refines the earlier failure: a photoreal FULL-BODY person in slot 1 is reproduced wholesale, while a FACE crop in slot 1 is used as a feature source. Order still matters for placement/composition; it is not a capability gate here.

cases.verdict: THE APPLICATION'S OWN GRAPH. This is the file produced by ComfyUIImageClient.BuildQwenImage21Workflow (the production graph builder), submitted UNCHANGED to the host with both references uploaded under their graph names â€” not a hand-built proof graph. Identity lands (the reference woman's face, freckles and top-bun) and the pose follows the skeleton's splayed arms and wide stance, which is exactly the shape the app sends once a native-reference render carries a pose. Replay: emit with QWEN21_EMIT_GRAPH/QWEN21_EMIT_PROMPT/QWEN21_EMIT_REFS, then helpers/local-comfyui-host/run-local-proof.ps1 -WorkflowPath <graph> -ImagesJsonPath <manifest>.

The previous verdict claimed a 3/4-right turn without measuring it; the render in fact faced LEFT (nose_offset_pct -15.73%) because angle-34-right.png was the same body pose as the left. Confirms the turn comes from the skeleton (the only input that changed).

cases.verdict: Identical to case 12 - mean absolute pixel difference 2.89/255 - so the face reference is REDUNDANT once the body reference is present. At full-body scale the accepted front already fixes identity, and the third slot buys nothing.

True full back view: back of the head with NO face visible, the accepted body build preserved, and the tree tattoo on her LEFT calf - i.e. no face and the correct side. The skeleton is DWPose-annotated from plateBack, whose face keypoints are a clump precisely because the face is hidden.

supported: Qwen-Image-2.1 reads an OpenPose skeleton in a native reference slot as POSE GUIDANCE - no ControlNet adapter is required for pose on this model.
Location + pose + identity compose in ONE native-reference call, in both portrait and wide frames.
An ANGLE-MATCHED (frontal) face reference transfers identity well; an angle-mismatched profile reference does not.
Slot order does not gate capability in a 3-reference composition.
notSupported: A photoreal full-body photograph in <image1> does NOT act as a pose donor - it is reproduced as the base image.
notTested: Precision of skeleton adherence (limb angles are approximate, not exact).
Ambiguous stances (lying, all-fours) through the native route; ControlNet itself fails on those.
More than one posed person in a single call (two skeletons + two faces).
Explicit/adult content behaviour of this composition.
